finding.title: A question card's options do not say what pressing them does as things stand
finding.what_the_person_sees: While the session ran, the card '"Add the club's phone number to contact.html": the specialist asks you' showed [Send answers] with no line, [Go ahead without] 'The specialist decides and says what it assumed.' and [Cancel task] 'Drops it. Nothing waits on it.'. Pressing Send answers then joined the running session. The Redo dialog likewise says only 'Reopens it; say what is wrong and the next attempt fixes it.'
finding.expected: C3 addition: each Inbox option says what pressing it does as things stand ('...; it joins the running session if it fits' or '...; it runs at your next Start'), as Try again's explain does. Design 3.8: Send answers 'The task goes on with your answers now'.
finding.evidence: c18-run.json cards[0].choices; screenshot /tmp/frbench/live4/session/s1/steps/36-c18-40-card-1-inbox-card.png; packages/runtime/src/daemon/request-words.ts:546 (fixed explain, no preparedExplain(ctx))
finding.repro: Bench s1 (bench-live): a coder task that needs a fact only the person has ('Add the club's phone number to contact.html') plus one more task; Start; when the question card arrives while the other task runs, open the Inbox.
finding.suspected_cause: questionsCard builds Go ahead without with a fixed explain, and Send answers has none; only the Try again, rework and conflict options use preparedExplain(ctx).

verdict.root_cause:
The finding is real. Both options on the specialist's questions card prepare work. Go ahead without and Send answers each call prepareAnswer, which calls prepareWork (packages/runtime/src/session/person-questions.ts:1051-1085 and the answered branch after it). Pressing either one therefore joins the running session if it fits, and otherwise waits for the next Start. The card does not say this before the press.

1. Go ahead without has a fixed explain, "The specialist decides and says what it assumed." (packages/runtime/src/daemon/request-words.ts:546). questionsCard never calls preparedExplain(ctx), even though requestContexts already gives it the prepared context (daemon/views.ts:976, wired in the C3 fix-up's B1). Only the retry/verdict card (:445-446), the failed card (:1143), the rebuild card (:1328) and the conflict card (:1714-1716) use preparedExplain(ctx).

2. Send answers cannot have an explain at all. RequestWords (request-words.ts:73-106) has no field for the form's submit button, and the reply is just 'form'. The UI's PersonQuestionsForm hard-codes a bare `<Button>Send answers</Button>` (apps/ui/src/pages/InboxPage.tsx:259-266). So the design §3.8 one-line consequence ("The task goes on with your answers now") never appears.

The live evidence matches the code exactly:
- c18-run.json, card 01a1e806-1dca: choices are only Go ahead without and Cancel task, with fixed explains, while sessionStatus is running.
- Screenshot 36: Send answers has no line.
- The Done line after the press does say "it joins the session that is running.", so the outcome words are fine. Only the words before the press are missing.

The second card ("Write the FAQ") shows the same thing. The fix-up's starts-words test covers only the Try again wording (starts-words.test.ts:72-107), so nothing caught the questions card.

The Redo aside is also real, but it sits outside the C3 addition's 'Inbox option' scope. The Tasks-row explains are static UI strings (apps/ui/src/lib/task-actions.ts:44-58). Make ready and Resume give both branches ('the running session takes it if it fits, else your next Start'). Redo ('Reopens it; say what is wrong and the next attempt fixes it.'), Try again and Go ahead without say nothing about what follows. The sentence after Redo does say 'It joins the session that is running.'
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/request-words.ts:546 (questionsCard's fixed Go ahead without explain; RequestWords :73-106 has no field for the form's submit); apps/ui/src/pages/InboxPage.tsx:259-266 (Send answers rendered with no explain); secondary: apps/ui/src/lib/task-actions.ts:44-58 (Redo/Try again/Go ahead without row explains)

finding.title: Make ready on a draft too big for the running session says it may join it
finding.what_the_person_sees: "Research local garden suppliers" is ready. It joins this session if budget is left after its own tasks, else your next Start.
finding.expected: Its estimate (about CHF 1.10) is above the whole session budget (CHF 1.00), so the line that is true now is 'it runs at your next Start' (design section 5 rule 4). It did not run; the end log read 'Left for your next Start: ... (about CHF 1.10)'.
finding.repro: While a CHF 1.00 session runs, press Make ready on a researcher draft whose outcome names five files.
finding.suspected_cause: prepareWork returns 'no_room' whenever a session runs, without comparing the task's estimate with what the session could ever give it.

verdict.root_cause: The running session's admit treats two different cases as one outcome. At runner.ts:2067-2072, when a task's estimate is above the whole work budget (`est > workBudgetUsdMicro`), the code's own comment says it "never joins (D4: it runs in its turn at the next Start)". It still returns the same `no_room` as a task that only lacks room right now (`est > room`). prepareWork (prepared-work.ts:131-132) turns that outcome into preparedLine("no_room") at prepared-work.ts:200-201: "Ready: it joins this session if budget is left after its own tasks, else your next Start." task.ts withNextLine/afterMove (commands/task.ts:1656-1677) adds that line after the Make ready sentence. The first clause can never come true for this task. The session's re-plan (runner.ts:2251) takes a newcomer only when `est <= workBudgetUsdMicro && est <= room`, so no budget left over after the session's own tasks ever lets it in. The evidence matches the code. The session budget was USD 1,250,000 (CHF 1.00), so the work budget was USD 1,000,000 (CHF 0.80). The draft was priced at USD 1,378,000 (session.left_for_next_start, about CHF 1.10). Its line still said it may join, and the session ended with "Left for your next Start". This breaks design section 5 rule 4 ("True now") and rule 9 ("No promises the code does not keep"). The finding's suspected cause is half right. prepareWork does not call no_room for every running session: it asks the session's admit, and admit compares the estimate with the work budget correctly. The bug is that admit then reports the result with the wrong outcome and words. The spec (runC-plan d1109-starts-engine: "an oversized task ... -> no_room (it cannot fit ...)") carried the same conflation.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:2069 (oversized and no-room-now share `no_room`); packages/runtime/src/session/prepared-work.ts:200-201 (the no_room words); packages/runtime/src/session/prepared-work.ts:106-111 (summarize)
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. In live-sessions.ts, add an AdmitOutcome `too_large`: the task's estimate is above the session's whole work budget, so it runs at the next Start.
2. In the runner's admit (runner.ts:2069), split the condition. `est > workBudgetUsdMicro` sets `too_large`; `est > room` keeps `no_room`. Both still record `asked` and keep D7's `before` handling.
3. In prepared-work.ts, add `too_large` to PrepareOutcome, preparedLine, isPreparedOutcome and preparedClause. Proposed line (at most 100 characters, true now): "Ready: it is larger than this session's budget, so it runs at your next Start." The plain "Ready: it runs at your next Start." would also be true.
4. In summarize: if every task is too_large, return too_large. If too_large is mixed with joined or no_room, do not return the may-join words for the too_large task. The simplest true choice is to treat too_large like `stopping` in the mixed case, or name the larger task.
5. Optional: previewWork and preparedExplain (the read-back and card explain) cannot see the estimate, so their general "if it fits" words stay as they are.
6. Update docs/maintainers for the starts engine and ADR 0118's outcome list.

finding.title: Inbox 'Answered' line for a specialist's questions still names the running session after it ended
finding.what_the_person_sees: After the session ended, Inbox > Answered: 'Answers saved in the decision record; "Add the club's phone number to contact.html" is done; what waits on it joins the session that is running.' (nothing waits on the task)
finding.expected: True now (design section 5 rule 4): no running session once it has ended, and no 'what waits on it' when nothing does.
finding.evidence: screenshot /tmp/frbench/live4/session/s1/steps/44-c18-60-inbox-answered-open.png; request-words.ts questionsOutcome rewrites the stored start outcome 'joined' against the task's current status
finding.repro: Answer a specialist's question while the session runs, let the session end, then open Inbox > Answered.
finding.suspected_cause: questionsOutcome words the stored start outcome against the task's status, never against the session's current state.

verdict.root_cause: questionsOutcome (request-words.ts:576-588) builds the Answered line from the start outcome saved when the person answered (card.start = "joined", meaning the task itself joined the session that was running then). It checks only the task's status now. When the task is done, the S-2 rewrite at :578-581 turns "it joins the session that is running" into "what waits on it joins the session that is running". That rewrite was written for the person's own task (card.on_answer === "done"), where the answer closes the task and the prepared work is what waits on it. A specialist's card has on_answer === "ready": the prepared work was the task itself, and that work is now finished. The rewrite never checks on_answer, never checks ctx.waiting (empty here; the open card said "Nothing waits on it"), and never checks whether a session still runs. requestContexts reads the running/prepared facts only for open cards (views.ts:1004), so an answered card cannot know the session ended. The same false clause appears on the "without" branch (:583-584) for a specialist's task finished after Go ahead without, and with waits_start ("what waits on it runs at your next Start"). Checked against the bench's state.sqlite (opened read-only): both C18 cards hold outcome "answered", start "joined", on_answer "ready". Both tasks are done, and no task depends on the phone-number task. A probe against the 4cf11fd code (/tmp/frbench/verify-L4-session-6/probe.ts) gives the screenshot's sentence word for word: 'Answers saved in the decision record; "Add the club's phone number to contact.html" is done; what waits on it joins the session that is running.' The person-task case still gives the intended "...; what waits on it runs at your next Start."
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/request-words.ts:578-588 (the S-2 rewrite at 578-581 and the done branches at 583-584 and 587-588); contributing: packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:1004 (no running or prepared facts are read for answered cards)
verdict.fix_sketch:
In questionsOutcome, once ctx.taskStatus === "done":
- Specialist's card (card.on_answer !== "done"): drop the start clause. What the answer started was the task's own work, and that work is over. Say 'Answers saved in the decision record; "X" is done.' and for without, '"X" is done without your answers.'
- Person's own task (on_answer === "done"): keep the "what waits on it ..." clause only while ctx.waiting is not empty. Do not repeat a stored "joined" ("joins the session that is running") unless the running state is read for answered cards too. For example, requestContexts passes running for a done person task with waiting work, or the clause is dropped once nothing waits.
Put the same guard in the matching retryOutcome "accept" branch if a review finds the same pattern. Keep the existing person-task test lines (inbox.test.tsx:973, real-daemon.test.ts:3524), which still hold.
verdict.failing_test_idea: real-daemon.test.ts (the person's boundary is GET /inbox through the client). Set up a project with one specialist task that nothing depends on. The bench stand-in asks a question during a running session. The person answers while the session runs, and the Done line reads '...goes on with them; it joins the session that is running.' Wait until the task is done and the session has ended. Then the Answered row's outcome for that card equals 'Answers saved in the decision record; "<task>" is done.' and contains neither "what waits on it" nor "session that is running". It fails today with the screenshot's sentence. Add a unit case in packages/runtime/test for requestWords: card {key: "person_questions:t", outcome: "answered", start: "joined", on_answer: "ready"}, ctx {taskStatus: "done", waiting: []}. Add a second unit case with outcome "without". The existing person-task cases (on_answer "done", waits_start, with a waiting dependant) stay as they are.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-starts-engine (S-2 prepared-outcome words; the rewrite came in 3a5981d)
verdict.notes: Evidence: steps/44-c18-60-inbox-answered-open.txt shows the same false line on both C18 cards, "Write the FAQ" too, although its card's task is done and nothing waits on it. The live Done lines at answer time (37-..., 39-...) were true then. The bug appears only when the card is shown again after the task finished. No leftover in L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 names it. C5L-C3-left-5 lists "a restart after an answered card (S-2)" only as a test gap of the continuation, so it is not this bug. I did not run the bench; the evidence is the read-only check of the stored state.sqlite plus the probe against the 4cf11fd code (/tmp/frbench/verify-L4-session-6/probe.ts, q.cjs). Severity: minor, not words-only. The sentence claims something false now: work waiting on the task, and a session running. It does this in the Answered history, which design §5 rule 4 covers, and nothing is lost or blocked.

finding.title: A done task's row no longer says what budget its cost counts against
finding.what_the_person_sees: Task A's row after it is done reads only 'CHF 0.02' (before the run it read 'of CHF 0.10 budget'); the drawer says 'spent CHF 0.02 of CHF 0.10 budget'.
finding.expected: Step branch (i): 'its row reads its cost with "of CHF 0.10 budget"'.
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/session/s1/steps/52-c32-42-tasks-after.png; c32-run.json drawerA.rowText; apps/ui/src/pages/project/TasksTab.tsx:563 hides TaskCap when isFinished(t)
finding.repro: Give a task Budget 0.10, run it to done, open the Tasks tab.
finding.suspected_cause: TaskCap is rendered only for unfinished tasks.

verdict.root_cause:
The observation is accurate. After task A is done, its row shows only 'CHF 0.02' (screenshot 52-c32-42-tasks-after.png; c32-run.json drawerA.rowText; capTitle null). The drawer reads 'spent CHF 0.02 of CHF 0.10 budget'. This is the designed behaviour, not a defect.

What the code does: TasksTab.tsx:562-564 renders TaskCap only when the task is neither finished nor a person's task. isFinished (task-actions.ts:214-217, doc comment 'Finished: no cap, no "waits for" edits, no cost limit line') returns true for done and cancelled. taskCapWords' doc comment (TasksTab.tsx:80) says 'for a task not done or cancelled'.

Each spec agrees with the code:
- docs/design/core-experience.md section 3.5 lists 'the cap line on finished tasks' under 'Must not show'.
- The d1116-budget-all design (/tmp/frbench/d1116-budget-all-design.json, its BA-9 test notes) says: "Keep 'never CHF 0.00' and 'no line on done or cancelled'".
- docs/maintainers/apps.md (tasks tab) says 'nothing on a done or cancelled one'.
- docs/user-guide.md:1254 says 'a done or cancelled task shows no limit'.
- apps/ui/test/tasks.test.tsx:206-208 tests it: 'A finished task has no cap line.'

The owner's answer of 2026-11-16 asks that 'the Tasks row, the drawer and Costs show one figure against the budget'. That holds: the row, the drawer and Costs > By task all show the same CHF 0.02 (spentChf 22922), and the drawer shows it against the CHF 0.10 budget.

The mistake is in the step text. Branch (i) of LC-C32 ('its row reads its cost with "of CHF 0.10 budget"') expects a line on a done row, which contradicts the design the step was written from. The loose phrase 'Each Tasks row reads its cost with "of CHF x budget"' in that design's Check in the app likely fed into it. The app did what it was designed to do. The model played no part.
verdict.where: apps/ui/src/pages/project/TasksTab.tsx:563 (isFinished(t) hides TaskCap), apps/ui/src/lib/task-actions.ts:215; spec at docs/design/core-experience.md section 3.5 'Must not show: ... the cap line on finished tasks'

No code fix. Correct the live-check step instead. LC-C32 branch (i) should read: 'A is done; its row reads its cost (the same figure as the drawer and Costs > By task) with no budget line under it, and the drawer reads "spent CHF x of CHF 0.10 budget"'. It would also update section 3.5, apps.md, the user guide and tasks.test.tsx:206-208.

verdict.notes: I verified this against the code and docs at 4cf11fd. I did not run the stand-in bench because the evidence and the code already settle it. Costs > By task, the row and the drawer show the same figure for A (CHF 0.02, spentChf 22922 out of a 100000 budget), which meets the LC-C32 pass line 'one figure' for each task. finding.title: 'Left to do: nothing the criteria require.' is read as one thing left to do, so finished research pauses with a card asking for more money instead of going to review
finding.what_the_person_sees:
The research was finished, but the person is asked to pay for another session to 'continue' it, and the screens say one thing is left to do when there is none.
- Inbox card: '"Compare three static site hosts ..." paused before this session's budget ran out', with 'Left to do • nothing the criteria require.' and the button 'Continue (CHF 0.40 more)'.
- Session log and task drawer: '... paused before this session's budget of CHF 0.40 ran out: it spent CHF 0.23 and listed one thing left to do.'
- Tasks row: 'Paused before the session's budget ran out'.
finding.expected: When a wrap-up report says the criteria need nothing more, the run goes to its review and can be done in the same session, with no pause card. This is the l3-handoff-checks / L3-research-1 rule: the session still had CHF 0.17 of its CHF 0.40, and a fifth is kept for reviews.
finding.evidence:
- Model-call log seq 8 (the researcher's last reply) ends: 'Where I stopped: `hosts.md` is complete and meets the three acceptance criteria as I read them. Nothing is half done. ...' and 'Left to do: nothing the criteria require.'
- Card lists: [{label:'Left to do', items:['nothing the criteria require.']}].
- Run outcome 'Paused'.
- parseHandoff() run read-only with tsx on the 4cf11fd checkout (/tmp/frbench/live4/pause/scripts/parse-check.mts):
  - 'Left to do: nothing the criteria require.' => ['nothing the criteria require.']
  - '- nothing the criteria require.' => ['nothing the criteria require.']
  - 'Left to do: nothing.' => []
  - 'Left to do: nothing for the criteria.' => []
- The continuing run's brief then said 'Left to do ... - "nothing the criteria require." Start with the first item of its list'. That run made no change, and the critic accepted the work. The extra session cost CHF 0.13 for this task.
finding.repro: On bench-live, make a researcher task estimated above the work budget (the researcher's starting estimate is about CHF 0.42) and start a session with CHF 0.40. When the real model ends its wrap-up with 'Left to do: nothing the criteria require.', the task pauses with a Continue card instead of being reviewed.
finding.suspected_cause: The NOTHING regex in packages/runtime/src/session/budget-pause.ts only accepts a 'nothing' followed by a preposition (for, in, by, to meet ...) or by punctuation. 'nothing the criteria require' has neither, so isNothing() is false and the line is kept as an item. The wrap-up instruction itself says '(only what the task's criteria still need, as a list with the next step first, or nothing ...)', which invites this phrasing.

verdict.root_cause: The "nothing" detector in parseHandoff has a fixed list of phrasings. `NOTHING` (budget-pause.ts:80-83) accepts nothing/none followed by (a) left/required/needed words, then (b) an ABOUT clause that has to start with a preposition (for, in, by, under, within, to meet/satisfy/...; :76), or (c) punctuation followed by a reason (AFTER, :78). A relative-clause form that has no preposition ("nothing [that] the criteria require", "nothing the task needs") matches none of these. So isNothing() (:92) is false, add() (:176-183) keeps the line, and leftToDo = ["nothing the criteria require."]. executor.ts:1725-1732 then sees result.wrapUpSent && parsed.leftToDo.length > 0 and sets stoppedBy "wrap_up", so the outcome is "paused" instead of a review. That gives the person the budget card with Continue, the log line "listed one thing left to do" (pauseSentence, budget-pause.ts:317), and a continuing brief (task-context.ts:160/218) that says "paused at a budget before its work was done" and "Start with the first item of its list: 'nothing the criteria require.'". The app itself prompts this phrasing: the wrap-up text the model hears (agent/loop.ts:109) and WRAP_UP_BRIEF_LINE (budget-pause.ts:53) both say "only what the task's criteria still need ... or nothing". ADR 0112 (lines 75-76, 339-348) says a "nothing" about the criteria is nothing and the run is reviewed. I reproduced this read-only with tsx on 4cf11fd. finding.title: The session's Details count the plan two ways: 'It promised 2 tasks', then '0 of 1 planned task done'
finding.what_the_person_sees:
Session page > Details shows three lines that count the plan differently:
- 'Plan: "Compare ..." (about CHF 0.42), larger than this session's work budget: it works until that budget is used. 2 ready tasks in priority order (1 item cut to fit the budget).'
- 'It promised 2 tasks, about CHF 0.32.'
- 'Session review measured: 0 of 1 planned task done; the planned tasks cost CHF 0.23 against an estimate of CHF 0.32.'
finding.expected: One count of what the session planned and promised, consistent across the Details lines (design section 5: no numbers that disagree).
finding.repro: Start a session with a larger task first and a small task after it (LC-C7) and open Details on the session page.

verdict.root_cause:
The code counts the task that waits behind the larger one (`after_large`) three different ways:
(1) In `cutPlanToBudget`, every `leftOutForBudget` item goes into the summary clause "(N item cut to fit the budget)", and that includes the `after_large` ones (runner.ts:5376-5380). So the Plan line says "2 ready tasks in priority order (1 item cut to fit the budget)". But the Start dialog, and OP-0's design, say that task is the session's own and "runs after it only if budget is left". It was never cut.
(2) The promise is built from `first = plan.items + afterLarge` (runner.ts:1731-1751) and emitted as session.promised (runner.ts:1844-1849). So "It promised 2 tasks, about CHF 0.32" counts 2. The 0.32 is only the larger task's room.
(3) The session review's planned set comes only from `planItemsOf(session.plan)`, which reads `plan.items` (critic/src/session-review.ts:136-156, :207 and :346-352). The `after_large` task is in `leftOutForBudget`/`promise`, not in `items`. So views.ts:854 prints "0 of 1 planned task done". The run indicator showed "(0 of 2 done)" during the same session.
I reproduced this with tsx against the code at 4cf11fd (/tmp/frbench/verify-L4-pause-3/cut.mts). `cutPlanToBudget([big 0.47, small 0.03], 0.355)` gives items `[big]`, `small` as `after_large`, and summary "2 ready tasks in priority order (1 item cut to fit the budget)". `describeEvent` then gives "It promised 2 tasks, about CHF 0.32." and "Session review measured: 0 of 1 planned task done; ..." for the same plan. These are exactly the three Details lines in the evidence. The app produced this deterministically. The model's choices played no part.

verdict.fix_sketch:
Use the promise as the one count for this kind of session.
(a) In `cutPlanToBudget`, count only the items left out for `no_room` or `after_others` in "(N cut to fit the budget)". Name the `after_large` items as the dialog does, e.g. "(1 comes after it if budget is left)", or drop the clause for them. The session.planned line then agrees with the dialog and the promise.
(b) In `loadSessionReviewData` and `runSessionReviewChecks`, make the planned set `plan.items` ∪ `plan.promise.taskIds` (at least the `after_large` ids; the promise is already stored on the plan row via setPlan). Then the metric reads "0 of 2 planned tasks done", like "It promised 2 tasks" and the run indicator's "(0 of 2 done)". Keep the estimate as the promise's figure (CHF 0.32). A promised task that never ran must not be graded as a plan defect, or "Plan item references a task" findings would start to fire.

It leaves out runs whose outcome is `paused` or `budget_exceeded` (ADR 0112: no failed try, no sample). Two ways to apply this:
(a) Leave every such run out of tries.
(b) Leave it out only when a later work run of the same task continued it. A pause that ended the task (cancelled) would then still count as a try.
Apply the same rule to runsByTask, runsByModel and the bySpecialist run set. Add `tries` to CostBucket in api-types.ts:1095 and to the fake daemon. CostsTab renders `${accepted} / ${tries} (%)`, with the tooltip "Accepted by the critic / tries; a run paused and continued is one try". finding.title: The Sessions row of a session that ended on questions shows two different counts
finding.what_the_person_sees: After the phone card was answered and that task was done, the row reads "\"Add the choir's phone number to…\" and \"Add the choir's rehearsal address to…\" needed your answer." over "08:19 · under a minute · 2 needed you · Ended: 1 task needs you · CHF 0.02 on your API key".
finding.expected: One count, or two counts clearly told apart (what the session ended with and what still waits now), so the row does not say 2 and 1 about the same thing.
finding.repro: End a session with two question cards open, answer one, open the project's Sessions tab.
finding.suspected_cause: The 'Ended: N task needs you' status seems to come from the tasks' current states, while '2 needed you' is the count at the session's end.

verdict.root_cause: One Sessions row reads two different moments. The gist and the task counts come from the record written when the session ended: handoff.outcome.needsYou held both tasks, so the row says "2 needed you" and '"…phone…" and "…rehearsal…" needed your answer.' The ended words come from what still waits now. The daemon passes blockedNow = stillBlocked (server.ts:1796), which drops the phone task because it is now done, and endedStatusText then prints "Ended: 1 task needs you". This was built on purpose: d1109-sessions decided "'Ended: 1 task needs you' stays true now" (L-21 rule, ADR 0116 rule 10, the same map as the session page's badge). Nobody thought about what happens when the row's past-tense counts sit next to it. The "Ended:" prefix makes the current count read as the count at the session's end, so the person sees 2 and 1 for the same thing. The live evidence matches the code. c19-b.json "after" shows the phone task done and the rehearsal task still needs_human. The second session's handoff has the phone task done. The row text in 72-c19-25-sessions-tab.txt is exactly countsWords + endedWords joined by SessionsTab.sessionRowLine.

In sessionRowView: when the session completed, its record has needsYou/failed/paused tasks, and waits (stillBlocked) is above zero, set endedWords to a "still" phrase such as "1 still needs you" (or "1 still needs you, 1 still paused"), not "Ended: 1 task needs you". When waits is zero after the person answered everything, keep "Done" (the row then reads "2 needed you · Done", which is already coherent). The row would read "08:19 · under a minute · 2 needed you · 1 still needs you · CHF 0.02 on your API key". When nothing changed since the end (waits equal to the end counts), the plain "Ended: 2 tasks need you" can stay, or the "still" form can be used everywhere for consistency. Put the phrase builder next to endedStatusText in stop-words.ts so there is still one map, and update the fake daemon (apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts around :9348) and the d1109-sessions maintainer doc and ADR 0116 rule 10 to say how the list tells the end and now apart.

finding.title: The Answered line reads 'is done; a session started for it'
finding.what_the_person_sees: Inbox > Answered: "Answers saved in the decision record; \"Add the choir's phone number to contact.html\" is done; a session started for it (this project starts by itself when work is ready)."
finding.expected: Events in the order they happened: your answers started a session for it and it is now done (design section 5). Related: L4-session-6, where the Answered line kept a stale 'is running'.
finding.repro: With the setting on, answer a question card, let the session finish, then open Answered.
finding.suspected_cause: The answered line puts the task's current state in front of the outcome that was kept when the card was answered.

verdict.root_cause: questionsOutcome builds the Answered line from the task's status now (ctx.taskStatus, which views.ts:1043 reads from the task when the list is shown) plus the start clause the card stored when it was answered. When the task is done, it writes `<task> is done` first and then adds the stored clause. Only prepared outcomes get rewritten to "what waits on it ..." (lines 578-581, isPreparedOutcome). The hands-off start is stored as start "started" with start_by "hands_off", which isPreparedOutcome does not cover. So startWords -> preparedClause gives "a session started for it (this project starts by itself when work is ready)", a clause about the task itself, and it lands after "is done". The line then puts the later event (done) before the earlier one (a session started for it), against design section 5 rule 2. The bench state confirms the stored card for the phone task is {outcome: answered, start: started, start_by: hands_off} with the task done. A tsx probe of requestWords with that card and taskStatus done prints the live line word for word.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/request-words.ts:569-591 (questionsOutcome; the done branch at :587-588 and `after` at :578-581); the clause comes from startWords :404-406 -> preparedClause in packages/runtime/src/session/prepared-work.ts:211-214,230-239
verdict.fix_sketch:
In questionsOutcome, when ctx.taskStatus === "done" and the stored start is a start rather than a prepared outcome ("started"/"queued", with or without start_by hands_off), write the events in the order they happened:
- On a specialist's card (the answer sent the task back to work), for example: `Answers sent: a session started for "X" by itself (this project starts by itself when work is ready); it is done.`
- On the person's own task (card.on_answer === "done", where the answer closed the task and the session ran what waits on it): `Answers saved in the decision record; "X" is done; a session started for what waits on it (this project starts by itself when work is ready).`
Apply the same rule to the "without" branch (:582-584), which gives "is done without your answers; a session started for it". Do it in one helper, e.g. doneThenStarted(card, ctx), used by every Done line that adds startWords after "is done". Also fix retryOutcome's accept branch (:494-499): with hands_off it currently produces the broken sentence `"T" is done; what comes after it a session started for it (...)`, because `.replace(/^it /, "")` assumes a clause that starts with "it ". Keep each line at 160 characters or fewer.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-starts-engine (owns startWords and the Done lines in request-words.ts, S-2/S-12)
verdict.notes:
The finding is real at 4cf11fd. I confirmed it with a read-only query of /tmp/frbench/live4/session/s1/home/data/state.sqlite (card 01a1e896-55db...: answered/started/hands_off, task done). A probe, /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-session-13/probe.ts, reproduces the exact Inbox text. While the task is running or ready, the same card reads correctly ("Answers sent: ... goes on with them; a session started for it ..."). The order only flips once the task is done.

Same-root siblings the fix should cover:
(1) A person's own task (on_answer done) under hands-off would read "is done; a session started for it". There "it" names the wrong thing: the session ran what waits on it.
(2) The "without" branch.
(3) retryOutcome accept with hands_off, where the probe /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-session-13/probe2.ts prints the ungrammatical '"T" is done; what comes after it a session started for it (...)'.

Related but different: L4-session-6. The Garden club lines in the same screenshot ('is done; what waits on it joins the session that is running') are a stale prepared clause, not an order problem.

No leftover in L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 names this. C3L-4 is about the hands-off setting's effect line, not the Answered line. I agree with severity "words": nothing is wrong in what happened, only the order of the words.

finding.what_the_person_sees: Inbox > Updates shows 'Your last session was interrupted when Forerunner closed. "Write a two-sentence welcome note for the bakery in welcome.md" is ready again.' with only 'Mark read'. The session page's last log line reads '08:36 Interrupted: Forerunner closed: nothing done. CHF 0.01.' Forerunner closed at 08:34; 08:36 is when it started again.
finding.expected: Design section 5 (Stop, crash 'after' example): '... is ready again. [Continue]'. The user guide only promises 'one line in the Inbox', and Start session in the header works. A log line's time should be when the thing happened, or the line should say Forerunner started again then.
finding.repro: Start a session on one small task. Kill the daemon's process group during the task's first model call. Start Forerunner two minutes later. Open the Inbox and the session page.
finding.suspected_cause: packages/runtime/src/session/recovery.ts posts the Update without a Continue action. The interrupted event is written at recovery time.

verdict.root_cause:
Both halves come from the code at 4cf11fd, not from the model.

(1) No Continue. recoverInterruptedSessions posts the crash news as a plain message: store.message.send with type "info" and a body only (recovery.ts:309-323). A message cannot carry an action at all. MessageRow (packages/state/src/types.ts:354-368) has no action, link or session field. The Inbox's Updates list (apps/ui/src/pages/InboxPage.tsx:700-723) renders MessageBody, the badges, the sender and time, and Mark read. finding.title: Just after the project budget is raised, Start says the paused task 'needs your answer', but there is no card
finding.what_the_person_sees: Ten seconds after raising the budget: 'Nothing can run: "Write the club motto in motto.txt" needs your answer.' with Open it, and no card in the Inbox. A minute later the task is Ready.
finding.expected: The task is ready at once, or the dialog says it goes on shortly.
finding.repro: Set project budget 0.06; a writer task pauses before its review; raise the budget to 0.50; open Start within 10 s.
finding.suspected_cause: The wake after the raise waits for the scheduler tick.

verdict.root_cause: Raising a limit does not wake the tasks paused at it. The only caller of `wakeBudgetWaits` is the scheduler's `refresh`, which runs before each tick (compose.ts:3963), and the tick comes every 30 s (`tickMs = 30_000`, session/triggers.ts:289). The `budget.set` run for a project only writes the project row (commands/budget.ts:362-368): it calls no wake and no prepare. Credentials are handled differently: `credentialSaved` wakes credential waits at once (compose.ts:4663). Until the next tick, the task stays `needs_human` and its budget_stop card stays open. The Start check's `needsYou` (server.ts:1606-1624) picks up that open card, and `startBlocked` (start-blocked.ts:185-190) then says 'Nothing can run: "X" needs your answer.' with Open it. The test suite expects this delay: budget-pause.test.ts:709 says 'The next tick wakes it' and calls `rt.scheduler.tick()` after the raise. The live state database confirms the timing. Raise applied at 09:32:57.486. Start dialog captured at 09:33:07.8, while the card was still open (the Overview in step 83 shows 'Needs you … paused at the project's budget of CHF 0.06 / Answer'). Tick at 09:33:16.822 withdrew the card (`outcome: went_on`) and set the task to ready. Inbox looked at 09:33:50, after the card was gone. So the delay is real, but the 'no card' part is a timing misreading: the card existed when the dialog named it, and the wait was 19 s, not 'a minute'. A second, smaller point: `needsYou` counts any open card on a `needs_human` task. A budget pause at an outer limit (only option: Cancel task; it 'goes on by itself once you raise that budget') is therefore read as 'needs your answer' even before any raise. The plan's comment meant only a pause that got no further, or a question.

finding.title: The run's start line ignores the project budget
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'This run may spend CHF 1.20: before a step that could take it past CHF 0.96 ...' under a project budget of CHF 0.06.
finding.expected: The line names the limit that actually applies.
finding.repro: Same as L4-l3-5, first Start.
finding.suspected_cause: The line uses the specialist's run limit.

verdict.root_cause: The run's start line comes from the run's own cap, and the project's budget and the month's cap are never part of that cap. executor.ts:1044 takes runCapOf(task, defaultSpec.maxBudgetUsdMicro). This task has no budget of its own, so that is the writer's per-run limit: USD 1.50 (evals/registry/specialists/writer-marketing/specialist.md:15), which is CHF 1.20. executor.ts:1071-1081 then takes the smaller of that and the session's work budget (CHF 5.00 x 0.8 = 4.00), so CHF 1.20 stays. runCapSource only knows task_budget, specialist_limit and session. executor.ts:1129 puts this figure into brief.budgetUsdMicro, and :1255 copies it into the run token's budgetUsdMicro. At the first model call, hooks.ts:160-166 calls SessionBudget.precheck(runId, claims.budgetUsdMicro, ...). budget.ts:247-252 fixes the wrap-up line from that cap with wrapUpLineOf: reserve 0.24, line 0.96. Only after that do hooks.ts:167-170 check the outer caps (caps.check: project, month, plan), and they only refuse a call; they never change the line. budget-pause.ts:358 then writes 'This run may spend CHF 1.20: before a step that could take it past CHF 0.96 ... reserve of CHF 0.24' while the project's budget is CHF 0.06. The evidence matches this exactly (cm-run1.json, all in one session): the session started with CHF 5.00, the writer's line said CHF 1.20, and the review then paused at 'the project's budget of CHF 0.06'. The wrong figure is more than a wording problem. The wrap-up line (0.96) sits far above the project's stop (0.06), so under a binding outer limit the run is never told to wrap up. It gets a hard stop instead ('its next step would have gone over'), and the line's promise of a reserve to finish is false. ADR 0112 point 6 says a stop names its real limit; the start line breaks that and points 3/4.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:1129 (brief.budgetUsdMicro = min(work.capUsdMicro, sessionLeftUsdMicro), no outer cap; runCapSource at :1081); packages/runtime/src/enforcement/hooks.ts:160-166 (the line is fixed from claims.budgetUsdMicro before caps.check at :167); packages/runtime/src/enforcement/budget.ts:247-252; packages/runtime/src/session/budget-pause.ts:358 (the words)

1. In LoopTaskExecutor.execute, beside sessionLeftUsdMicro (executor.ts:1071), read what the outer limits still allow for this run's scope, together with the level that binds (project or month; for plan share, its room). Use the stop line, not the 80% room that callRoomUsdMicro uses: for example a CapsPort.remainingUsdMicro(scope, phase) that returns { usdMicro, level }, or CapChecker.check's remaining and level.
2. Make brief.budgetUsdMicro the smaller of work.capUsdMicro, sessionLeftUsdMicro and that outer remainder. When the outer remainder is the smallest, set runCapSource to 'project' or 'month'. The token, the wrap-up line, the reserve and the stop sentence then all follow from one figure, and the run hears the wrap-up inside the project's budget.
3. Optionally let budgetLineWords name a limit that is not the run's own ('This run may spend CHF 0.06, what is left of the project's budget: ...'), as limitWords already does for stops.
4. Open point for the owner, as with BA-4: whether a run under a binding outer limit should keep room in it for its review. Today the review paused at the project's budget.

finding.title: Session review words do not match what the session did
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'Session review: accepted (grade 100, 0 findings).' beside '0 of 1 planned task done' in three sessions whose only task paused. 'Session review: sent back for changes (grade 85, 1 finding).' on a session whose task was done; the finding is an overrun note.
finding.expected: Words that say what waits, and never 'sent back' for a session.
finding.evidence: cm-run1.json, ph-run.json, rg-run2.json, swiss.json; Reviews › Session checks: '85 / 100 sent back ... over their estimate of CHF 0.07 by 51%, with one task tried twice'
finding.repro: A session whose only task pauses; a session whose task overruns its estimate.
finding.suspected_cause: Verdict 'revise' is mapped to 'sent back' except in the two cases L3-run-8 fixed.

verdict.root_cause:
The finding has two halves, and only the second one holds up.

(1) A session whose only task paused reads "accepted (grade 100, 0 findings)". This is by design, not a defect. Wave 7's R-sessreview (L7S-5) chose this on purpose:
- packages/critic/src/session-review.ts:449-466 (onlyPaused) records no finding for such a session.
- docs/maintainers/critic.md:431-436 says the same.
- budget-pause.test.ts:406-415 and event-lines.test.ts:425-427 assert it.
- Live check 3's own L3-run-8 entry named "Session review: accepted" for the paused case as the wording to copy.
The line also sits only under the session page's Details, below the log line '... paused before its review: ...'.

(2) "Sent back for changes" on a session whose only task was done is real. The session review reuses the task review's verdict words. Two lines of the code produce it:
- sessionChecks makes any medium finding blocking (session-review.ts:586, `isBlocking(findings) ? "revise"`).
- The overrun note is a medium finding (session-review.ts:417-423: "Planned tasks cost ..., over their estimate ... with one task tried twice").

So a done session that overran its estimate by more than 50% gets the verdict "revise", and two places turn that into "sent back":
- The session log: views.ts:876 prints `waits ?? verdictWords(verdict)`, where verdictWords("revise") is "sent back for changes" (event-lines.ts:421-422).
- The Reviews tab: ReviewItem shows verdictLabel(r.verdict) for session checks too (ReviewsTab.tsx:108, plain-words.ts:83-84: "sent back"). Its finding badge also says "to fix" (findingStateWords).

L3-run-8 replaced these words only for two cases (runner.ts:4379-4388, waitsFor answers or decision), and only in the log line. A session verdict sends nothing back: the runner and compose do nothing with "revise".

Reproduced by importing the code at 4cf11fd (/tmp/frbench/l4-l3-7/check.mts). One task done, tried twice, CHF 0.07 against a CHF 0.04 estimate:
- Result: verdict revise, grade 85, one medium finding "Planned tasks cost CHF 0.07, over their estimate of CHF 0.04 by 57%, with one task tried twice".

(1) Budget card, "Left to do". parseHandoff caps every item at 200 characters with `cut` (budget-pause.ts:146 and :207, MAX_ITEM_CHARS=200 at :57). `cut` breaks inside a word. The live state shows this: card.left[0] in l3b's state.sqlite is exactly 200 characters and ends in "... plus a short introduction. Put cl…". The display step, cardItem (request-words.ts:227-238, called from pausedWorkLists :985), sees the stored "…", drops the broken word and keeps the ellipsis, so the person reads "Put…". cardItem also cuts at 220 with cutWords, so a long item never shows whole. The comment on budget-card.ts:170-176 and runtime.md:2453 say "each item whole", but the 200-character bound on the parsed handoff is still there. The wrap-up words (loop.ts:109, budget-pause.ts:53) never ask the model to keep items short, so a long item from the model is expected, not a model fault. The same cut item also goes into the continuation brief (task-context.ts:163, quote(t, 200)), so the next run loses the end of its own next step.

(2) Failed-task card, "It reported: ...". emptyChangeSummary (pr-executor.ts:612-624) takes the report's first sentence and cuts it at a word past 160 characters. So the "first sentence" runs on to "...(the git status check below shows whether anything actually changed)." That is over 160 characters, so it is cut to "(the git status check below shows…", which also leaves a parenthesis open. With a correct split the first sentence is 'Summary: kite/club.txt already existed with one line, "The kite club meets on Sundays."' (about 85 characters), which fits whole.

finding.what_the_person_sees: 'read README.md', then 'Told the writer to wrap up: it spent CHF 0.06 ...'; the card says 'No files created or changed.' CHF 0.08 spent, nothing written, no reason given.
finding.expected: A line saying the step was cut, and the writer told to write in parts.
finding.evidence: Model-call log seq 33: max_tokens 6308, stopReason max_tokens, USD 0.065244, no tool call
finding.repro: Same as L4-l3-14.
finding.suspected_cause: The budget caps max_tokens, and a one-call write of a long file is truncated.

verdict.root_cause:
The evidence checks out (l3b/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl, run 01a1e8f5-d110, the second seq 33 in the file): max_tokens 6308, stop max_tokens, 6308 output tokens, USD 0.065244, no text and no tool call. The session's own events (state.sqlite, session 01a1e8f5-d08b) go from 'read README.md' (seq 11) straight to 'Told the writer to wrap up' (seq 12). The code explains each part.

(1) The cap comes from the budget, as designed (W15-13). A file-writing run's call may use only the money below the run's wrap-up line (loop.ts:640-659: room = line - spent - searches, then fitMaxTokens). Line CHF 0.06 minus USD 0.0075 already spent gives 6308 tokens, and that one reply used all of the money below the line.

(2) The cut reply had nothing it could keep, so the loop asks again (loop.ts:910-947). The retry's cap cannot be raised, because no money is left below the line. loop.ts:647-649 checks `!wrapUpSent` before beforeModelCall decides on the wrap-up, so the reserve never pays for the retry and seq 34 gets the 4096 floor. The same request carries both the cut note and 'Wrap up now'. Because the reply showed no blocks, `where` is 'before it said anything' (loop.ts:920). That picks 'Answer again, more briefly.' (loop.ts:1335-1336), not the 'one file per call, short enough to fit' wording. Two different causes look the same here, and the log cannot tell them apart: hidden thinking (call-log.ts:302-330 does not record thinking_delta), or a write_file whose tool_use_end never came (collectStream drops it, types.ts:457).

(3) No log line. The loop reports the cut only as a bare `warning` RunEvent (loop.ts:943-946). The executor's onEvent (executor.ts:1442-1520) turns budget_line, web_search*, wrap_up_sent, model_call_end and tool events into steps, but has no branch for `warning`. compose.ts:3624 ignores it too. The person sees no line, and the CHF 0.05 call shows up only as spend (runner.ts:2728). The budget pause card is built from the handoff alone ('No files created or changed'), so it never gives the reason. The only mention is in the model's own report ('My previous attempt hit the output limit and produced nothing'), which the card does not show. This breaks design §3.7 and §4.14 ('Each model and tool call ... emits one step line').

Paying for a cut reply and not using it is by design (U-085: 'Every call is billed, the cut ones included'). The model's choice to spend 6308 tokens in one reply is its own. But the missing line and the wrong-variant note are app behaviour, so this is not the model alone.

- the card's `why` and `title` (budget-card.ts:261, 270),

finding.title: Read-backs for same-titled tasks drop '(the older one)'; the resume read-back states the result before Yes
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'Pause "Write the guide"? ...'; 'Resume "Write the guide"? It is ready again. It runs at your next Start.'
finding.expected: Say which task, and describe the outcome in the future tense before Yes.
finding.repro: Two tasks named 'Write the guide'; pause and resume the older one from chat.
finding.suspected_cause: The read-back uses the title only.

verdict.root_cause:
The finding is half right.

Part 1 is real. A move's read-back and its after-Yes line name the task by its title only, so when two tasks share a title the person cannot tell which one Yes will change. `findTask` (task.ts:243-288) uses the person's word to pick the right task at :261-263, but it returns a bare TaskRow and the word is lost. After that, `moveCard` (task.ts:1627-1649) builds `ask: moveAsk(task, ...)` and `sentence: moveSentence(task, ...)`. Both build their text from `const t = quote(task.title)` (moveAsk :509, moveSentence :572), which gives 'Pause "Write the guide"? No session runs it until you press Resume.' (:537), 'Resume "Write the guide"? It is ready again.' (:542), 'Paused "Write the guide": ...' (:580) and '"Write the guide" is ready again.' (:586). `task.transition`'s card (:1280-1301) has the same gap. The evidence confirms the app's own deterministic text: gc-p.json and gc-r.json show "calls": [] and usd 0, so no model call was made, and the person's "(the older one)" appears in neither the read-back nor the line after Yes. The user guide (docs/user-guide.md:322-325) says two same-titled tasks "are named apart in Chat by what tells them apart", and design §5 rule 3 asks for names that identify. Run L3's l3-small fix fixed which task the word picks (L3-run-6). Its own check_in_the_app step expected the read-back 'Resume "Write the guide"? …', so this gap was left untouched, not brought back by a later change.

Part 2 is not a defect. The Resume read-back's 'It is ready again. It runs at your next Start.' follows the design. Its first sentence is the design's own consequence line for Resume (core-experience.md:147: "It is ready again; the next session can run it."). The second comes from withPreview (task.ts:1681-1695), which drops 'Ready: ' from previewWork's line. The design writes every consequence line in the present tense to say what Yes does ('No session runs it until you press Resume.', 'Drops it.', §5 Move dialog). A future tense would be a change to the design, not a bug fix.
verdict.where: packages/commands/src/commands/task.ts:509 (moveAsk quotes the title only), :572 (moveSentence the same), :1647 (moveCard's ask), :262 (findTask drops the word that picked the task); design core-experience.md:147 for the Resume consequence line
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. Add a helper in task.ts, say `taskLabel(ctx, task)`. It returns quote(title) when no other task of the project has the same `sameTitle()`. Otherwise it returns quote(title) plus the tag that tells this task apart: "#17" when each task in the group has its own pull request, else the age tag in brackets, "(the older one)". Use the age tag, not the state tag: it is the only kind that stays the same from read-back to after-Yes line to Undo, since a state tag changes when the move does ("the ready one" becomes "the paused one"). Simpler still: reuse the person's own word when it picked the task.
2. Pass the label into moveAsk and moveSentence as an optional `name` that replaces `t`. Do this from moveCard, from task.transition's plan and run, and from the move's undoSentence.
3. A task with a unique title keeps 'Pause "X"? …' exactly.
